Wall Detection

BoobaStudio's Wall Detection feature uses computer vision to automatically detect and place walls on your battle maps. This tool analyzes the scene background image to find edges—like walls, doors, and obstacles—and converts them into Foundry VTT wall segments.

Overview

Wall Detection uses OpenCV.js, a powerful computer vision library, to process your map image and extract edge information. The detected edges are converted into wall segments that you can preview, edit, and then apply to your scene.

How It Works

  • Image Analysis: The scene background is loaded and preprocessed
  • Edge Detection: OpenCV's Canny edge detection finds boundaries in the image
  • Contour Extraction: Edges are converted to polygon contours
  • Wall Generation: Contours are simplified into straight line segments
  • Preview & Edit: You can review and modify detected walls before applying
  • Apply to Scene: Confirmed walls are created as Foundry Wall documents

Opening Wall Detection

There are several ways to access the Wall Detection tool:

From Canvas Controls (Recommended)

  • Open your scene in the canvas
  • Click the Walls Layer icon in the left toolbar (the wall/brick icon)
  • In the wall tools that appear, look for the BoobaStudio Wall Detection button
  • Click it to open the Wall Detection panel

From Scene Context Menu

  • In the Scenes sidebar, right-click on any scene
  • Select Detect Walls from the context menu
  • The scene will activate and the Wall Detection panel will open

From BoobaStudio menu

  • Open the BoobaStudio radial menu (click the BoobaStudio coin or use your configured hotkey)
  • Navigate to the utility/tools section
  • Select the wall detection option

From Welcome Screen

  • Open the BoobaStudio welcome/onboarding screen
  • Click the Wall Detection card in the features grid

Detection Parameters

The sliders in the Options panel control how edges are detected:

Blur Kernel (1-21)

Controls the amount of Gaussian blur applied before edge detection.

  • Lower values (1-5): Preserve fine details, detect more edges including noise
  • Higher values (9-21): Smooth out noise, detect only prominent edges
  • Recommended: 5 for most maps, 3 for high-detail maps, 9+ for noisy images

Close Kernel (1-15)

Morphological closing operation that connects nearby edges.

  • Lower values (1-3): Keep edges separate, more segments
  • Higher values (5-15): Merge gaps, create continuous walls
  • Recommended: 3 for clean maps, 5+ for maps with broken lines

Canny Threshold 1 (0-255)

Lower threshold for the Canny edge detector's hysteresis procedure.

  • Lower values (20-50): More sensitive, detects faint edges
  • Higher values (80-150): Less sensitive, only strong edges
  • Recommended: 50 for standard maps, lower for faded/light maps

Canny Threshold 2 (0-255)

Upper threshold for the Canny edge detector.

  • Should be higher than Threshold 1
  • Controls which edges are considered "strong"
  • Recommended: 150 (about 3x Threshold 1)

Min Contour Area (0-5000)

Minimum pixel area for a detected contour to be kept.

  • Lower values (20-50): Keep small shapes (furniture, details)
  • Higher values (200-1000): Only keep large structures (rooms, walls)
  • Recommended: 50 for detailed maps, 200+ to reduce clutter

Min Segment Length (0-100)

Minimum length in pixels for a wall segment.

  • Lower values (3-6): Keep short segments (corners, details)
  • Higher values (15-30): Only keep longer wall sections
  • Recommended: 6 for accuracy, 15+ for simpler wall layouts

Presets

Quick-access presets for common map types:

PresetBest ForSettings
DefaultGeneral purpose mapsBalanced settings
High DetailMaps with fine details, furnitureLow blur, sensitive detection
Simple/CleanClean digital maps, vector artHigh blur, strong edges only
Dungeon MapClassic dungeon crawlsOptimized for stone corridors

You can also save your own presets using the save button in the toolbar.

Wall Types

When walls are detected, you can assign them different types:

Tools

Select Tool ()

Click on detected wall segments to select them. Selected segments can be deleted or have their type changed.

Eraser Tool ()

Click and drag to remove wall segments in an area. Adjust the eraser brush size with the slider.

Brush Tool ()

Draw new wall segments manually by clicking and dragging on the canvas.

Area Select Tool ()

Draw rectangular regions to restrict detection to specific areas of the map.

Color Detection

Enable Color Detection to detect walls based on specific colors in your map:

  • Toggle "Enable Color Detection"
  • Add colors using the color picker or eyedropper tool ()
  • Adjust the color threshold (how similar colors must be to match)
  • Only edges matching these colors will be detected

Useful for maps where walls are drawn in a specific color.

Image Source Options

Use Texture

When enabled, uses the scene's foreground texture instead of the background image. Useful for maps with separate wall/floor layers.

Enable Downscaling

Automatically reduces large images for faster processing. Recommended for maps over 4000px. Disable only if you need maximum precision on detailed maps.

Live Preview

When enabled, detected walls are shown as colored overlays on the canvas before you apply them. This lets you adjust parameters and see results in real-time.

Workflow Tips

  • Start with a preset that matches your map type
  • Adjust Canny thresholds first—they have the biggest impact
  • Use Min Segment Length to filter out noise
  • Preview before applying to catch unwanted walls
  • Use the eraser to clean up false positives
  • Apply in stages for complex maps—detect rooms, then furniture

Troubleshooting

Too many walls detected

  • Increase Blur Kernel
  • Increase Canny thresholds
  • Increase Min Contour Area and Min Segment Length

Missing walls

  • Decrease Canny thresholds
  • Decrease Blur Kernel
  • Check if walls have enough contrast with the floor

Walls in wrong places

  • Try Color Detection to target specific colors
  • Use Area Select to limit detection regions
  • Manual cleanup with Eraser tool

Performance issues

  • Enable Downscaling for large images
  • Reduce Max Segments in settings
  • Close other applications
